findings.title: Default proto codec now rejects legacy (non-ProtoReflect) v1 messages
findings.why_it_matters: Any application whose RPC messages are legacy v1-only generated types (no ProtoReflect method, e.g. old protoc-gen-go or gogo output) used to marshal/unmarshal through the default codec because github.com/golang/protobuf proto.Message is the v1 interface (Reset/String/ProtoMessage) and its Marshal wraps legacy messages. After the import swap, v.(proto.Message) asserts the v2 interface that requires ProtoReflect, so every such RPC fails with 'failed to marshal, message is %T, want proto.Message'. This is a silent public behavior regression of the default codec, contrary to the 'behavior should be preserved' intent; repo's own reflection/grpc_testing_not_regenerate/testv3.go types have zero ProtoReflect methods and are exactly this shape. Converting via protoadapt.MessageV2Of (accepting protoadapt.MessageV1) in both Marshal and Unmarshal preserves legacy support.
findings.suggested_fix: In codec.Marshal/Unmarshal accept v1 or v2 messages: add helper messageV2Of(v any) proto.Message that returns v if it is proto.Message, else protoadapt.MessageV2Of(v.(protoadapt.MessageV1)) (error if neither), then call proto.Marshal/Unmarshal on the result. Add a test with a legacy-only message.
evidence: encoding/proto/proto.go:41 -- vv, ok := v.(proto.Message)   (import now "google.golang.org/protobuf/proto"; previously "github.com/golang/protobuf/proto")
gomodcache golang/protobuf@v1.5.3/proto/proto.go:50 -- type Message = protoiface.MessageV1 (v1 interface, no ProtoReflect)
reflection/grpc_testing_not_regenerate/testv3.go contains 0 occurrences of ProtoReflect (legacy message shape)

findings.title: Invalid load_reporting_interval error reports a stale nil err
findings.why_it_matters: When the management server sends an invalid (or missing) load_reporting_interval, the client logs 'invalid load_reporting_interval: <nil>' instead of the validation reason. The rewrite from ptypes.Duration (which returned the error) to a bare CheckValid() != nil discards the error, and the %v formats the outer err from stream.Recv(), which is always nil at this point. Operators lose the only diagnostic for a misconfigured LRS server. Validation semantics themselves (nil/out-of-range rejected) are preserved.
findings.suggested_fix: Capture the error: rInterval := resp.GetLoadReportingInterval(); if err := rInterval.CheckValid(); err != nil { return nil, 0, fmt.Errorf("invalid load_reporting_interval: %v", err) }
evidence:
xds/internal/xdsclient/transport/loadreport.go:174-175 -- if rInterval.CheckValid() != nil {
		return nil, 0, fmt.Errorf("invalid load_reporting_interval: %v", err)
xds/internal/xdsclient/transport/loadreport.go:165-168 -- resp, err := stream.Recv(); if err != nil { return nil, 0, ... } so err is nil at line 175

residual_risks: test/tools/go.mod downgrades golang.org/x/tools v0.17.0 -> v0.14.0 and adds x/sys v0.13.0 / x/sync v0.4.0 (go.sum) while leaving x/mod v0.14.0 and x/exp/typeparams 20240119 untouched; unrelated to the proto migration and not verifiable offline (module lookup disabled). It silently pins the goimports/vet tooling used by vet.sh to an older release; confirm this was intentional (go mod tidy artifact) and that `go run golang.org/x/tools/cmd/goimports` and staticcheck still resolve.

status.Details() now returns anypb.UnmarshalNew results and different error text (e.g. protoimpl error 'invalid empty type URL' instead of 'message type url "" is invalid'); callers matching on the error string, or consuming legacy v1-registered detail types (previously unwrapped to the v1 value via ptypes.DynamicAny), may observe a different dynamic type/message. Not demonstrated for any in-repo caller.

internal/pretty.ToJSON v1 branch switched from jsonpb.Marshaler{Indent} to protojson.MarshalOptions{Indent}; no unit test covers pretty output, so any log-format drift (e.g. Any resolution, field naming) is unverified. Reasoned equivalent for generated messages.
testing_gaps: No test exercises encoding/proto codec with a legacy v1-only message, which is why the codec regression passes the suite (go test ./encoding/... passes).
No test covers recvFirstLoadStatsResponse error text for an invalid load_reporting_interval.
